newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola down sharply on commercials, funds, CBT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola down sharply on commercials, funds, CBT.

text.p: WCE canola and flax futures traded down or near the C$10 a tonne lower limit and set new contract lows in canola on commercial and fund selling spurred by a USDA crop report.

"Commercials sold July, funds sold August and November. We are down on the USDA report," a trader said. The USDA forecast U.S. soybean acreage at 70.85 million acres, more than expected by U.S. traders. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -1.70 Monday from -3.14 Friday. July-Nov spread at $26, July-Aug $9.50.
July and August fell the C$10 limit to $373 and $365.80, respectively, both new contract lows while November fell $8.30 to $348.50 after it set a low of $346.50.
July flax fell $6.40 to $331.50, September fell $9.50 to $302 after hitting commission sell stops, November fell $7.90 to set a new low of $297 on commercial selling.
PCTS and locals bought 140 December feed wheat down $0.20 to $153.50, October fell $0.20 to a new low of $153.10.
July western barley fell $0.50 to a new low of $122.50 and October sank $0.70 to a new low of $126.60 on commercial sales.
Feed peas and oats were offered by commercials but none traded.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, peas.)
